g.e: Con we (noi) il verbo be è are: we are.

g.q: This is Anna. ___ is my teacher.
g.e: Anna è una donna, quindi usiamo she (lei).
Con I (io) il verbo be è sempre am: I am (I'm).

g.q: My bag is new. ___ is red.
g.e: Per una cosa o un animale si usa it.
Con they (loro) il verbo be è are: they are (they're).

g.q: Marco and I are friends. ___ are in the same class.
g.e: Marco and I (Marco e io) = we (noi).

v.q: The day after Monday is ___.
Saturday and Sunday are the ___.
v.e: Sabato e domenica = the weekend (il fine settimana).

v.q: Twelve and three is ___.
Which number is 18?
v.e: 18 = eighteen. I numeri 13-19 finiscono in -teen. Eighty è 80.

v.q: The day before Saturday is F___.
Write the number 11 in words.

s: I am a student in Bagheria.
She is my friend from school.
We are in class on Monday.
It is Friday today!

g.e: Nella domanda il verbo va prima del soggetto. Con you si usa are: Are you...?
La negazione di he is è he isn't (he is not).

g.q: Is she a teacher? No, she ___.
g.e: Risposta breve negativa: No, she isn't.
Nelle domande: parola interrogativa + are + soggetto: Where are you from?
La negazione con I è I'm not (I am not). Non si dice I amn't.

g.q: ___ (they / be) at home? Yes, they are.
g.e: Nella domanda il verbo va prima: Are they...?

v.q: Paris is in ___.
Tokyo is in ___.
Which number is 40?
Which number is 99?
Madrid is in S___.
Write the number 55 in words.

s: Are you from Italy or Spain?
No, I'm not from England.
Is your teacher from London?
We aren't British, we're Italian.

g.e: I (io) → my (mio): my name is...
Your = tuo/vostro. You're = you are, non è un aggettivo possessivo.

g.q: My brother is ten. ___ name is Marco.
g.e: Per un uomo o un ragazzo si usa his (suo, di lui).
We (noi) → our (nostro).

g.q: Mr and Mrs Russo live in Palermo. ___ house is big. (they)
g.e: They (loro) → their (loro): their house.

g.q: This is Giulia and this is ___ book. (she)
g.e: Per una donna o una ragazza si usa her (suo, di lei).

v.q: ___ your books at page twelve.
v.e: Open your books = aprite i libri.

v.q: ___ to the audio.
v.e: Listen to = ascoltare. Listen to the audio.

v.q: How do you ___ Palermo? P-A-L-E-R-M-O.
v.e: Spell = fare lo spelling, dire le lettere una per una.

v.q: You want the teacher to talk more slowly. What do you say?
o: Can you speak more slowly, please?
Can you close the door, please?
v.e: Speak more slowly = parlare più lentamente.

v.q: Work with a p___ (= another student).
v.e: Partner = compagno con cui lavori in coppia.

v.q: ___ the door, please. It's cold. (≠ open)
v.e: Il contrario di open (aprire) è close o shut (chiudere).

s: What's your name and email address?
Can you repeat that, please?
Open your books and look at the picture.
Their teacher is very nice.

g.e: Le parole che finiscono in -ch prendono -es al plurale: watches.

g.q: There are three ___ in my bag.
g.e: Vocale + y: aggiungi solo -s. key → keys.

g.q: My grandparents live in two different ___.
g.e: Consonante + y: la y diventa -ies. city → cities.
Man ha un plurale irregolare: men.
Molte parole in -fe/-f fanno -ves al plurale: knife → knives.
Child ha un plurale irregolare: children.

v.q: You use it to open a door: a ___
v.e: Key = chiave. Si usa per aprire la porta.

v.q: Il gatto è sotto il tavolo: The cat is ___ the table.
v.e: Under = sotto. On = sopra, in = dentro.

v.q: Le chiavi sono dentro la borsa: The keys are ___ the bag.
You put money and cards in it: a ___
Use it when it rains: an u___
v.e: Umbrella = ombrello. Inizia con vocale, quindi an umbrella.

v.q: Il libro è sopra il tavolo: The book is ___ the table.
v.e: On = sopra (a contatto con la superficie).

s: My keys are in my bag.
The glasses are on the table.
There are two umbrellas under the chair.
Where are my sunglasses?

g.e: In inglese l'aggettivo va prima del nome: a red car.
Gli aggettivi non cambiano al plurale: nice people.
Gli aggettivi non prendono la -s: my shoes are new.
Ordine: a + very + aggettivo + nome: a very big house.

g.q: Put the words in order: car / Italian / an
g.e: Articolo + aggettivo + nome: an Italian car.

g.q: Put the words in order: dog / big / a
g.e: L'aggettivo va prima del nome: a big dog.

v.q: Bananas are ___.
The opposite of expensive is ___.
The opposite of long is ___.
Which word means molto?
The opposite of old (for a person) is y___.
Red and white make p___.

s: My new phone is really expensive.
She has a very nice red car.
This film is quite good.
Her eyes are big and brown.

g.e: Imperativo negativo: Don't + verbo. Don't touch!
Per proporre qualcosa: Let's + verbo base (facciamo...).

o: Let's to go to the beach.
g.e: Dopo let's si usa il verbo base, senza to e senza -ing.

g.q: Please ___ quiet. The baby is sleeping.
g.e: L'imperativo usa il verbo base: be quiet (stai zitto).
Imperativo negativo: Don't + be. Don't be late!
Let's + verbo base: Let's play (giochiamo).

v.q: I want to eat. I'm ___.
I want a glass of water. I'm ___.
I'm very ___. I want to go to bed.
My exam is tomorrow and I'm not ready. I'm ___.
Non ho niente da fare: I'm b___.
The opposite of sad is h___.

s: Don't worry, it's an easy test.
I'm tired, let's go home.
Let's have a pizza, I'm hungry!
Please be quiet in the library.

g.e: Con he, she, it il verbo prende la -s: he works.
Negativo con I, you, we, they: don't + verbo.
Verbi in -ch, -sh, -s, -x prendono -es: she watches.
Con he/she/it: doesn't + verbo base (senza -s).
Consonante + y: y diventa -ies. study → studies.
Con she: doesn't + verbo base: she doesn't eat.

v.q: I ___ my homework after school.
v.e: Si dice do homework (fare i compiti), non make.

v.q: My parents ___ a lot of coffee.
v.e: Drink = bere. Si beve il caffè.

v.q: Do you ___ Italian or English?
v.e: Per le lingue si usa speak: speak Italian.

v.q: They ___ in a flat in Palermo.
I w___ TV every evening.
She p___ the piano. (suona)
v.e: Play the piano = suonare il piano. Con she: plays.

s: My sister lives in a flat in Palermo.
I don't eat meat, but I eat fish.
He watches TV after dinner.
We play football on Saturday.

g.e: Domanda con I, you, we, they: Do + soggetto + verbo.
Domanda con he, she, it: Does + soggetto + verbo.

g.q: Does your mum work at the weekend? No, she ___.
g.e: Risposta breve con she: No, she doesn't.
Dopo does il verbo è base, senza -s: Does he work?
Domanda: Do + they + verbo base.
Where + does + soggetto + verbo base.

v.q: A ___ works in a hospital and helps doctors.
A ___ flies planes.
A ___ works in a restaurant and brings you your food.
A ___ builds houses.
He works in a shop. He's a s___ assistant.
She writes for a newspaper. She's a j___.

s: Does your father work in a hospital?
What does your sister do?
Do you work at the weekend?
My mother is a doctor in Palermo.

g.e: Ordine: parola interrogativa + do + soggetto + verbo.

o: What time does the film start?
What time does start the film?
g.e: Ordine: What time + does + soggetto + verbo base.
Con be: parola interrogativa + is + soggetto.
What + do + you + do. Il primo do è l'ausiliare, il secondo è il verbo fare.

g.q: Put the words in order: you / like / do / pizza / ?
g.e: Do + soggetto + verbo + resto: Do you like pizza?

g.q: Put the words in order: she / where / work / does / ?
g.e: Parola interrogativa + does + soggetto + verbo base.

v.q: ___ do you live? In Bagheria.
___ is your birthday? In May.
___ do you study English? Because I want to travel.
v.e: Why = perché (domanda). La risposta inizia con because.

v.q: ___ brothers and sisters do you have? Two.
v.e: How many = quanti, con i nomi numerabili.

v.q: ___ is your teacher? Mr Smith.
___ old are you? I'm twelve.

s: Where do your parents live?
What time do you get up?
Why do you want to learn English?
How many languages do you speak?

g.e: Per il possesso: nome + 's. Marco's bike = la bici di Marco.
Whose = di chi. Who's = who is.

g.q: My ___ house is in Palermo. (i miei genitori)
g.e: Plurale in -s: si aggiunge solo l'apostrofo. parents' = dei genitori.
Possessore + 's + cosa: my father's car.

g.q: Il telefono di Sara: Is this ___ phone?
g.e: In inglese si dice Sara's phone, non the phone of Sara.

g.q: Il cane di mia sorella: my ___ dog
g.e: Possessore + 's: my sister's dog.

v.q: My mother's mother is my ___.
My father's brother is my ___.
My aunt's children are my ___.
My brother's daughter is my ___.
v.e: Niece = nipote (femmina, figlia di fratello o sorella).

v.q: My mother and father are my p___.
My sister's son is my n___.
v.e: Nephew = nipote (maschio, figlio di fratello o sorella).

s: Whose phone is this on the table?
My brother's wife is very nice.
My cousins live near my grandparents.
This is my aunt's house in Bagheria.

g.e: Con le ore si usa at: at seven o'clock.

g.q: We go to the beach ___ Sunday.
g.e: Con i giorni si usa on: on Sunday.
Con i mesi si usa in: in March.
Con go (movimento verso un luogo) si usa to: go to school.
Si dice at home (a casa), at school, at work.

g.q: I do my homework ___ the evening.
g.e: In the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening. Ma: at night.

v.q: I ___ up at seven.
I ___ a shower before breakfast.
v.e: Si dice have a shower (fare la doccia).

v.q: I ___ to bed at ten o'clock.
v.e: Go to bed = andare a letto.

v.q: After school I ___ home by bus.
I g___ dressed quickly in the morning.
In the evening I have d___ with my family.

s: I get up early in the morning.
We have lunch at home on Sunday.
She goes to work by bus.
I go to bed late on Saturday.

g.e: Con be l'avverbio di frequenza va dopo il verbo: I am always late.
Con gli altri verbi l'avverbio va prima del verbo: she never eats.
Once a week = una volta alla settimana. Va a fine frase.
Con be l'avverbio va dopo: he is hardly ever late (quasi mai).

g.q: Put the words in order: often / we / swim
g.e: Soggetto + avverbio + verbo: we often swim.

g.q: Put the words in order: sometimes / late / I'm
g.e: Con be l'avverbio va dopo il verbo. Sometimes può andare anche all'inizio.

v.q: The month after March is ___.
Christmas is in ___.
Which word means every time (100%)?
v.e: Always = sempre (100%). Usually = di solito, sometimes = a volte.

v.q: Never means ___.
v.e: Never = mai. Always = sempre, often = spesso.

v.q: The first month of the year is J___.
v.e: January = gennaio. I mesi in inglese hanno la maiuscola.

v.q: Every seven days = once a w___
v.e: Once a week = una volta alla settimana.

s: We usually go to the beach in August.
She is always happy in the summer.
I hardly ever watch TV.
My birthday is in January.

g.q: I ___ swim very well. I'm in a swimming team.
g.e: Can = sapere/potere. Nuoto bene, quindi I can swim.
Can è uguale per tutte le persone e va senza to: she can play.
Domanda: Can + soggetto + verbo. Non si usa do.
Dopo can't si usa il verbo base, senza to e senza -s.

g.q: Sorry, I ___ (can / not) come to your party.
g.e: Negativo di can: can't (cannot).
Nelle domande can va prima del soggetto: Can you...?

v.q: I ___ a taxi to go to the airport.
v.e: Call a taxi = chiamare un taxi.

v.q: Can you ___ my plants when I'm on holiday?
v.e: Water the plants = annaffiare le piante.

v.q: I can't ___ my keys! Where are they?
v.e: Find = trovare. Non trovo le chiavi!

v.q: Let's ___ a photo of the sea!
v.e: Si dice take a photo (fare una foto).

v.q: I b___ a newspaper every morning. (compro)
Please don't f___ your homework! (dimenticare)

s: Can you play the piano?
I can't find my phone.
She can speak English and French.
Can you help me with my homework?

g.e: Azione in corso adesso: be + verbo + -ing. The baby is crying.

g.q: They ___ football in the park now.
g.e: Con they: are + -ing. They are playing.
Domanda al present continuous: What are you doing?
Negativo: am/is/are + not + verbo in -ing.

g.q: She ___ (read) a book at the moment.
g.e: At the moment = adesso: she is reading.
Domanda: Is + it + verbo in -ing.

v.q: A dog ___.
My phone is ___. Can you answer it?
Don't ___! I can hear you.
The baby is ___ because it's hungry.
My grandfather s___ when he sleeps. It's very noisy!
At the end of the concert people c___. (applaudono)

s: The neighbours are playing loud music.
Why is the dog barking?
The baby is crying again.
I'm not sleeping, I'm reading.

g.q: I usually ___ to school, but today I'm going by car.
g.e: Usually = abitudine: present simple. I usually walk.
Look! = succede adesso: present continuous.
Every Tuesday = abitudine: present simple, she studies.

o: Sorry, I have dinner at the moment.
Sorry, I'm having dinner at the moment.
Sorry, I having dinner at the moment.
g.e: At the moment = adesso: present continuous, I'm having.

g.q: We ___ (go) to the beach every summer.
g.e: Every summer = abitudine: present simple.
Now = adesso: present continuous, is sleeping.

v.q: Take your umbrella. It's ___.
It's zero degrees. It's very ___.
The season after spring is ___.
Il cielo è nuvoloso: It's ___.
v.e: Cloudy = nuvoloso. Windy = ventoso, foggy = nebbioso.

v.q: In Sicily it's very h___ in August.
The season before winter is a___.

s: It's raining, so I'm staying at home.
In summer it's very hot in Sicily.
Look, the sun is shining today!
We usually go skiing in winter.

g.q: I like Anna, but she doesn't like ___.
g.e: Dopo il verbo si usa il pronome complemento: me.
Complemento per un uomo: him (lui, lo).

g.q: My grandparents are great. I visit ___ every Sunday.
g.e: Complemento di they: them (li, loro).

g.q: Can you help ___, please? We're lost.
g.e: Complemento di we: us (ci, noi).

g.q: This is my sister. Do you know ___? (she)
g.e: Complemento di she: her (la, lei).

g.q: I have a new bike. I love ___! (it)
g.e: Per le cose il complemento è it, uguale al soggetto.

v.q: ___ day, a young man arrived in the village.
v.e: One day = un giorno. Si usa per iniziare una storia.

v.q: Everything was quiet. ___, there was a loud noise!
He looked everywhere and, in the ___, he found his dog.
Decide means ___.
First he opened the door, t___ he went in.
The opposite of arrive is l___.
v.e: Arrive = arrivare, leave = partire, andare via.

s: Can you help me with this bag?
I don't know him, but I like her.
Call us when you arrive.
Suddenly the man stopped and smiled.

g.e: Dopo love, like, hate si usa spesso il verbo in -ing.
Like + verbo in -ing: like getting up.
Like + -ing. Swim raddoppia la m: swimming.
Hate + -ing. Homework non ha il plurale.
Like + -ing: likes playing (va bene anche likes to play).
Don't mind (non mi dispiace) + verbo in -ing.

v.q: Which is correct?
o: My birthday is on the twelfth of May.
My birthday is in the twelve of May.
My birthday is at the twelfth May.
v.e: Date: on + the + ordinale + of + mese.

v.q: Write 5th in words.

s: I love going to the beach in summer.
Do you like cooking for your family?
She hates getting up early.
What's the date today?

g.e: Con un verbo normale (like) la domanda usa do: Do you like...?
Senza altro verbo si usa be: Is she a singer?
Con il verbo play il negativo usa don't: they don't play.
Present continuous: is + soggetto + verbo in -ing.
Interested è un aggettivo, quindi si usa be: Are you interested?

g.q: What kind of music ___ your parents like? (be or do?)
g.e: Like è un verbo normale: What... do + soggetto + like?

v.q: A person who plays the guitar is a ___.
A person who plays the piano is a ___.
Mozart wrote ___ music.
A group of musicians who play pop or rock music together is a ___.
v.e: Band = gruppo musicale. Team è per lo sport.

v.q: A person who sings is a s___.
She plays the d___ in a rock band. (la batteria)

s: Do you play a musical instrument?
Are you a fan of rock music?
My sister is a very good singer.
I don't like classical music.

g.e: Al passato di be, con I, he, she, it si usa was: I was.
Con we, you, they al passato si usa were. Last weekend indica il passato.

g.q: ___ your parents at home last night?
g.e: Nelle domande al passato con be si inverte: Were + soggetto plurale (your parents).

o: She weren't at school on Monday.
She wasn't at school on Monday.
She not was at school on Monday.
g.e: Negativo di was: wasn't (was not). Con she si usa was, non were.
Il film = it, quindi was; al negativo wasn't (was not).
Con you al passato si usa sempre were: Where were you?

v.q: Someone who paints is a ___.
v.e: Molti nomi di persona si formano con -er: paint → painter.

v.q: A person who plays the violin is a ___.
v.e: Per molti strumenti si aggiunge -ist: violin → violinist.

v.q: Tom Hanks is a famous ___.
v.e: Act → actor (con -or, non -er). Acting è l'attività, non la persona.

v.q: A ___ writes books.
v.e: Write → writer: chi scrive. Si toglie la -e e si aggiunge -er.

v.q: Someone who sings is a ___.
v.e: Sing + -er = singer, la persona che canta.

v.q: A person who plays the guitar is a ___.
v.e: Guitar + -ist = guitarist, come violinist e pianist.

s: My grandparents were very happy yesterday.
Where were you last Saturday?
I was at home with my family.
Her father was a famous painter.

g.q: We ___ football in the park yesterday.
g.e: Yesterday = passato. I verbi regolari prendono -ed: play → played.
Negativo: didn't + verbo base (senza -ed): didn't watch.
Domanda al passato: Did + soggetto + verbo base: Did you visit?
Consonante + y: la y diventa i e si aggiunge -ed: study → studied.

g.q: They ___ (arrive) in Palermo at nine o'clock yesterday.
g.e: Se il verbo finisce in -e si aggiunge solo -d: arrive → arrived.

g.q: He ___ (stop) the car outside the school ten minutes ago.
g.e: Verbi brevi con consonante-vocale-consonante raddoppiano: stop → stopped.

v.q: I saw her ___ week.
v.e: Last + week/month/year/night: last week = la settimana scorsa.

v.q: We moved to Bagheria three years ___.
v.e: Ago va DOPO il periodo di tempo: three years ago = tre anni fa.

v.q: I called you ___ morning.
v.e: Si dice yesterday morning / afternoon / evening, ma last night.

v.q: Today is Wednesday. The day before yesterday was ___.
v.e: The day before yesterday = l'altro ieri. Ieri era martedì, l'altro ieri lunedì.

v.q: I finished my homework l___ night.
v.e: Si dice last night (ieri sera), non yesterday night.

v.q: My brother phoned me two hours a___.
v.e: Ago = fa. Si mette dopo il tempo: two hours ago.

s: I watched a film last night.
We walked to the beach yesterday afternoon.
She started school two years ago.
Did you play tennis last weekend?

g.e: Go è irregolare: il passato è went, non goed.

g.q: We ___ a great time at the party last night.
g.e: Have è irregolare: il passato è had.

g.q: She ___ a new mobile phone for her birthday last year.
g.e: Get è irregolare: il passato è got.
Dopo did si usa sempre il verbo base: Did you go?
Negativo al passato: didn't + verbo base, anche per i verbi irregolari.

g.q: They ___ (buy) some arancine at the café yesterday.
g.e: Buy è irregolare: il passato è bought.

v.q: I ___ a shower every morning.
v.e: Si dice have a shower, have breakfast, have lunch (non make).

v.q: We ___ a taxi to the airport.
v.e: Get a taxi / a bus / a train = prendere un mezzo.

v.q: Let's ___ for a walk on the beach.
v.e: Go for a walk = andare a fare una passeggiata.

v.q: Did you ___ a good time in London?
I usually g___ up at seven o'clock.
On Saturdays we g___ shopping in Palermo.
v.e: Go shopping = andare a fare shopping (go + -ing).

s: I went to the beach with my friends.
We had pizza for dinner last night.
What time did you get home?
She got a nice present for her birthday.

g.q: The police ___ the man at the station yesterday.
g.e: Stop raddoppia la p: stopped. Yesterday indica il passato.

g.q: She ___ the door and ___ into the room.
g.e: Open è regolare (opened); come è irregolare (came).

g.q: What ___ you do after dinner last night?
g.e: Domanda al passato: What did you do? Did + verbo base.
Dopo didn't si usa il verbo base: didn't hear.
Take è irregolare: il passato è took.

g.q: Last week I ___ (not know) his name.
g.e: Negativo: didn't + verbo base: didn't know.

v.q: The past simple of leave is ___.
The past simple of think is ___.
v.e: Think è irregolare: think → thought. Thank è un altro verbo (ringraziare).

v.q: The past simple of find is ___.
The past simple of hear is ___.
v.e: Hear è irregolare: hear → heard (si aggiunge solo -d).

v.q: The past simple of say is ___.
I ___ (lose) my keys yesterday.

s: The police found the bag in the park.
I heard a strange noise last night.
She left the house very early.
Where did you go on Saturday evening?

g.q: There ___ a big kitchen in my flat.
g.e: There is + singolare (a kitchen). There are + plurale.

g.q: There are ___ chairs in the garden.
g.e: Nelle frasi affermative con il plurale si usa some.

g.q: There aren't ___ windows in the bathroom.
g.e: Nelle frasi negative con il plurale si usa any.
Two bedrooms è plurale, quindi there are.
Domanda con singolare: Is there a garage?

g.q: There ___ (not be) any plants in the living room.
g.e: Plants è plurale: negativo there aren't (are not) any.

v.q: We cook in the ___.
You sleep in the ___.
We park the car in the ___.
v.e: Garage = garage, dove si mette la macchina.

v.q: A ___ is on the floor. You walk on it.
v.e: Carpet = tappeto/moquette, sta sul pavimento. Ceiling = soffitto.

v.q: You go up the s___ to the first floor.
We watch TV in the l___ room.

s: There is a big garden behind our house.
Are there any shops near your flat?
There aren't any pictures in my bedroom.
We usually have dinner in the kitchen.

g.q: There ___ a lot of people at the beach yesterday.
g.e: People è plurale; al passato si usa there were.

g.q: There ___ a strange noise last night.
g.e: A noise è singolare; al passato: there was.

g.q: ___ there any cars in the street?
g.e: Cars è plurale: nella domanda al passato si usa Were there...?

o: There weren't any milk in the fridge.
There wasn't any milk in the fridge.
There wasn't some milk in the fridge.
g.e: Milk è non numerabile (singolare): wasn't. Nel negativo si usa any.

g.q: There ___ (not be) a TV in our hotel room last summer.
g.e: A TV è singolare e last summer indica il passato: there wasn't (was not).

g.q: Fifty years ago there ___ (be) three small shops in my grandfather's village.
g.e: Three shops è plurale e fifty years ago indica il passato: there were.

v.q: The keys are ___ my bag. I can't see them.
v.e: In = dentro. Le chiavi sono dentro la borsa.

v.q: She walked ___ the stairs from the ground floor to the first floor.
v.e: Dal piano terra al primo piano si sale: up the stairs.

v.q: The chemist's is ___ the bank and the bakery.
v.e: Between = tra due cose: between A and B.

v.q: Which means 'davanti a'?
v.e: In front of = davanti a. Behind = dietro. Next to = accanto a.

v.q: He came o___ of the house.
v.e: Out of = fuori da (movimento verso l'esterno).

v.q: The boy walked i___ the classroom and sat down.

s: There was a big bed in the room.
Were there any people in the garden?
He walked across the street to the park.
The bank is between the bakery and the chemist.

g.e: Apple inizia con suono vocalico: an apple.
Water è non numerabile: non si usa a/an, ma some.
Nelle frasi negative si usa any. Bread è non numerabile, quindi niente a.
Rice (riso) non si conta: non ha plurale. Eggs e bananas si contano.

g.q: I eat ___ egg every morning. (a / an)
g.e: Egg inizia con vocale: an egg.

g.q: There isn't ___ cheese in the fridge. (some / any)
g.e: Nelle frasi negative si usa any.

v.q: Arancine are made with ___.
v.e: Le arancine sono fatte di riso: rice.

v.q: Which one is a vegetable?
v.e: Carrot = carota, una verdura. Strawberry = fragola (frutta).

v.q: Which one is a drink?
Which one is fruit?
v.e: Pear = pera, un frutto. Onion = cipolla (verdura).

v.q: Tuna and salmon are types of f___.
v.e: Tuna (tonno) e salmon (salmone) sono pesci: fish.

v.q: Cows give us m___.

s: I'd like some water, please.
Are there any eggs in the fridge?
We had fish and salad for lunch.
Is there any cheese on the pizza?

g.e: Sugar è non numerabile: How much?

g.q: How ___ brothers and sisters have you got?
g.e: Brothers e sisters sono numerabili plurali: How many?
Chocolate è non numerabile; nelle frasi negative si usa much.
A lot of va bene con tutti i nomi. Many e a few solo con i numerabili.

g.q: How ___ (much / many) coffee do you drink?
g.e: Coffee è non numerabile: How much?

g.q: There are only a f___ apples left.
g.e: A few = alcuni, pochi (con i nomi numerabili plurali).

v.q: a ___ of jam
v.e: Jar = barattolo di vetro: a jar of jam.

v.q: a ___ of tuna
v.e: Tin = scatoletta: a tin of tuna.

v.q: a ___ of crisps
v.e: Packet = pacchetto: a packet of crisps.

v.q: a ___ of water
v.e: Bottle = bottiglia: a bottle of water.

v.q: a t___ of tomatoes
v.e: Tin = scatola di latta: a tin of tomatoes (pomodori pelati).

v.q: a j___ of honey
v.e: Jar = barattolo: a jar of honey.

s: How much water do you drink every day?
I bought a packet of biscuits at the market.
How many eggs do we need?
There's a jar of honey in the cupboard.

g.e: Aggettivi corti: + -er. Big raddoppia la g: bigger.
Tall è corto: taller than.

g.q: This book is ___ than the film.
g.e: Aggettivi lunghi: more + aggettivo: more interesting.

o: Today is more bad than yesterday.
g.e: Bad è irregolare: bad → worse.

g.q: The sea is ___ (hot) in August than in May.
g.e: Hot raddoppia la t: hotter.

g.q: This exercise is ___ (easy) than the last one.
g.e: Aggettivi in -y: la y diventa i + -er: easier.

v.q: How do you say 350?
v.e: In inglese britannico si mette and dopo hundred; hundred non prende la -s.

v.q: How do you write two thousand and twelve?
How do you say 7,500?
v.e: Thousand e hundred non prendono la -s dopo un numero.

v.q: Write 1,000 in words: one ___

s: My brother is taller than my father.
Is Palermo bigger than Bagheria?
The summer here is hotter than in London.
This book is more interesting than the film.

g.q: It's the ___ building in the city.
g.e: Superlativo degli aggettivi corti: the + -est: the tallest.

g.q: She is the ___ student in the class.
g.e: Aggettivi lunghi: the most + aggettivo.

g.q: Yesterday was the ___ day of my life!
g.e: Good è irregolare: good → better → the best.

o: It's the most big city in Italy.
It's the bigger city in Italy.
It's the biggest city in Italy.
g.e: Big è corto: the biggest (con doppia g).

g.q: This is the ___ (bad) pizza in town!
g.e: Bad è irregolare: bad → worse → the worst.

g.q: August is the ___ (hot) month of the year.
g.e: Hot raddoppia la t: the hottest.

v.q: You can see old paintings in a ___.
You catch a train at the ___.
A ___ is a very old building with strong walls and towers, where kings and queens lived.
v.e: Castle = castello, dove vivevano re e regine.

v.q: You borrow books from a ___.
v.e: Library = biblioteca (falso amico!). Bookshop = libreria, dove si comprano.

v.q: People pray in a c___.
A b___ goes over a river.

s: This is the oldest church in the town.
What's the most beautiful place in Sicily?
The museum is next to the town hall.
The market is the busiest place on Saturday.

g.q: I ___ going to visit my cousins.
g.e: Be going to: con I si usa am: I am (I'm) going to.

g.q: They ___ going to stay in a hotel.
g.e: Con they si usa are: they are (they're) going to.

g.q: ___ you going to take the train?
g.e: Domanda: Are + soggetto + going to + verbo.

o: We going to see the castle tomorrow.
We're going to see the castle tomorrow.
We're go to see the castle tomorrow.
g.e: Serve be (are) + going to + verbo base.
Going to + verbo base: going to take.

g.q: What are you going to do n___ weekend?
g.e: Next weekend = il prossimo fine settimana (senza the).

v.q: We ___ a lot of photos of the cathedral.
v.e: In inglese si dice take a photo (non make).

v.q: We want to ___ a hotel room for three nights.
v.e: Book = prenotare: book a room, book a table.

v.q: A ___ is a book with information about a city for tourists.
We ___ around the old town and looked at the shops.
We're going to go s___ in Rome.
v.e: Go sightseeing = visitare i luoghi turistici.

v.q: I'm going to buy a s___ for my grandmother. (a small present from a place you visit)

s: We're going to visit the museum tomorrow morning.
Are you going to take a lot of photos?
I'm going to stay with my cousins next summer.
They aren't going to go shopping tonight.

g.q: Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain.
g.e: Previsione basata su ciò che vediamo: It is (It's) going to rain.
You + are: You're going to fall.

g.q: He's very tired. He ___ win the race.
g.e: Con he: isn't (is not) going to.

o: I think she going to pass the exam.
I think she's going to pass the exam.
I think she's going pass the exam.
g.e: Serve is ('s) + going to + verbo base.

g.q: It's very late. We ___ (be going to / miss) the train!
g.e: We + are + going to + verbo base: we're going to miss.

g.q: Look at the blue sky. It ___ (be going to / not rain) today.
g.e: Negativo: it isn't going to + verbo base.

v.q: They're going to ___ married next year.
I'd like to ___ around the world.
v.e: Travel around the world = viaggiare per il mondo.

v.q: My family is going to ___ house. Our new flat is in Palermo.
One day she's going to ___ a famous singer.
They met at university and f___ in love.
v.e: Fall in love = innamorarsi. Al passato: fell in love.

v.q: My aunt wants to h___ children.

s: Look at the sky! It's going to rain.
I think you're going to travel a lot.
They're going to get married in June.
Be careful, you're going to fall!

g.e: Good è aggettivo; l'avverbio è irregolare: well.
Per descrivere come si fa un'azione si usa l'avverbio: careful + -ly.
Fast è irregolare: l'avverbio è uguale all'aggettivo, fast.
Prima di un aggettivo si usa l'avverbio (incredibly). Boring = noioso.
Aggettivo + -ly = avverbio: slow → slowly.

g.q: They played ___ (bad) and lost the match.
g.e: Bad → badly (avverbio di modo).

v.q: I lost my keys but, ___, my brother had another one.
We waited for an hour and ___ the bus arrived.
I love Sicilian food, ___ cannoli.
Which word means 'purtroppo'?
Come here i___! It's urgent.
We always do our homework t___.

s: She speaks English really well.
Please drive slowly near the school.
Luckily, the weather was very good.
We finally arrived at the hotel.

g.e: Dopo want si usa to + infinito: want to buy.
Dopo decide si usa to + infinito.
Dopo need si usa to + infinito.

o: I'd like to go to London.
g.e: Dopo would like si usa to + infinito.

g.q: They're planning ___ (visit) Rome in the summer.
g.e: Dopo plan si usa to + infinito.
Forget to do = dimenticare di fare.

v.q: I ___ to pass my exam. I studied a lot!
v.e: Hope to = sperare di. Enjoy e mind non vogliono to + infinito.

v.q: Please ___ to close the windows before you go out.
My little brother is ___ to swim.
He ___ to help me with my homework.
I'm going to t___ to call her later.
v.e: Try to = provare a, cercare di.

v.q: What do you w___ to do this weekend?

s: I want to learn to swim this summer.
We decided to go to the beach.
Don't forget to do your homework.
Would you like to come to my party?

g.e: Per parlare in generale non si usa the: Dogs are...

g.q: I usually go to ___ bed very late.
g.e: Si dice go to bed, go to school, go to work senza the.
The per una cosa specifica che conosciamo: la porta di questa stanza.

o: We have lunch at home on Sundays.
We have the lunch at home on Sundays.
We have a lunch at home on Sundays.
g.e: Con i pasti (breakfast, lunch, dinner) non si usa l'articolo.

g.q: Is there a chemist's near here? - Yes, ___ chemist's is next to the bank.
g.e: La seconda volta che parliamo di una cosa usiamo the.
The name of = il nome di (una cosa specifica).

v.q: I need to ___ my phone. The battery is low.
Can you ___ me the photos?
I ___ a new app yesterday.
You need a ___ to log in to the website.
I s___ for information on the internet.
Can you send me a t___ message later?

s: The internet is very slow today.
I need to charge my phone.
Can you send me the photos, please?
I often watch films on my phone.

g.e: Present perfect: have/has + participio. Con I si usa have.
Con he, she, it si usa has.
Domanda al present perfect: Have + you + participio.

o: I've never flew in a plane.
I've never flown in a plane.
I never have flown in a plane.
g.e: Dopo have si usa il participio passato: flown.
Negativo: haven't + participio.
Participio di lose: lost.

v.q: The past participle of eat is ___.
v.e: Eat - ate - eaten. Ate è il past simple.

v.q: The past participle of write is ___.
The past participle of see is ___.
The past participle of be is ___.
I've never ___ (drive) a car.
Have you ___ (read) this book?
v.e: Read - read - read: si scrive uguale ma il participio si pronuncia /red/.

s: I've never been to London.
Have you ever eaten arancine?
She has seen that film many times.
We haven't finished our homework yet.

g.q: I've been to Rome. I ___ there in 2019.
g.e: Con un momento preciso nel passato (in 2019) si usa il past simple.

g.q: Have you ever met a famous person? - Yes, I ___ one last year.
g.e: Last year = momento preciso: past simple (met).
Con When si usa il past simple: When did you go?
Con yesterday si usa il past simple, non il present perfect.

g.q: Have you ever been to Venice? - Yes, I ___ (go) last summer.
g.e: Last summer = passato preciso: past simple went.
Esperienza nella vita, senza tempo preciso: present perfect.

v.q: go - went - ___
buy - ___ - bought
v.e: Buy - bought - bought. Brought viene da bring.

v.q: Which verb has the same past simple and past participle?
v.e: Make - made - made. Take - took - taken; give - gave - given.

v.q: speak - spoke - ___
fly - flew - ___
break - ___ - broken

s: I've never swum in the sea at night.
We went to Palermo last Saturday.
Have you ever broken your arm?
She bought a new phone yesterday.

g.e: Present simple con you: Where do you live?
Con he, she, it (the film) si usa does.

g.q: Where ___ you go on holiday last year?
g.e: Domanda al past simple: did + soggetto + verbo base.
Ordine: parola interrogativa + did + soggetto + verbo.
Con be al passato non si usa did: Were you tired?

g.q: ___ you like pizza? - Yes, I love it!
g.e: Domanda al present simple con you: Do + you + verbo base. La risposta (I love it) è al presente.

v.q: ___ is your birthday? - In May.
___ is that girl? - She's my cousin.
___ do you like English? - Because it's fun!
v.e: Why = perché (nella domanda). Si risponde con because.

v.q: ___ old are you?
v.e: How old are you? = Quanti anni hai?

v.q: W___ bag is yours, the red one or the blue one?
v.e: Which = quale, quando c'è una scelta tra poche cose.

v.q: H___ often do you go to the cinema?
v.e: How often = ogni quanto, con che frequenza.

s: Where did you go last weekend?
What time do you usually get up?
Why do you want to learn English?
How often do you go to the beach?
